uncited: This family addresses the ill-posed inverse problem of tomographic reconstruction by replacing or augmenting traditional discrete voxel grids with neural networks, leveraging their expressive power to recover 3D density fields from sparse, noisy, or limited-angle projections.
**Backward Projection (Adjoint):** Distributing the error from the 2D detector plane back into the 3D volume.

The application of deep learning to tomographic reconstruction emerged as a response to the limitations of traditional analytical (e.g., FDK) and iterative algebraic methods (e.g., SART, SIRT) in handling sparse data, noise, and computational complexity.

While early deep learning approaches focused on post-processing or direct image-to-image mapping, recent developments emphasize end-to-end differentiable pipelines where neural networks serve as the volume representation itself (Implicit Neural Representations) or as powerful regularizers within the optimization loop.
This shift allows for the recovery of high-frequency details and robust performance under severe data scarcity, such as limited-angle or low-dose scenarios.
